Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the thoughtful questions. As promised, below is a concise recap of the performance / SLO discussion and proposed next steps so we can align on MAP items. Let me know if I missed anything.

SLO targets (as discussed):
- Latency: p95 <= 250 ms for single-turn requests (95th percentile), p99 <= 500 ms as an upper bound.
- Throughput: sustained 200 requests/sec, with burst tolerance to 400 rps for 1–2 minutes.
- Concurrency: target concurrency ~40 simultaneous inferences.
- Streaming: yes — need chunked streaming responses for long chat sessions; first-byte target < 150 ms when streaming enabled.
- Availability: 99.9% monthly uptime target for production traffic.

Technical notes / clarifications we need from your side to size Dedicated / routing policy:
1) Typical request payload size (avg tokens in prompt + expected response length).
2) Peak traffic window duration and expected daily traffic patterns.
3) Any strict regional or VPC/on-prem constraints.
4) Retention / logging requirements for KV cache and debug traces.

Attachments: I attached the SLO checklist and a simple template MAP (fintechco-demo-slo-checklist.xlsx).

Next steps I suggest this week:
- Marcus to run a short load test with our reference client (I can coordinate kickoff).
- You to confirm average token sizes and peak window timing.
- Quick sync (30m) Tuesday to review results and narrow Dedicated sizing.

Thanks — Ill loop Marcus on the next note for the tech details.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — this looks right. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Avg prompt + expected response: ~120 tokens input, ~220 tokens output (we have a mix of short commands and longer conversational flows).
- Peak: typically end-of-month batch runs between 09:00–11:00 PT for reconciliation flows; external chat traffic peaks around 14:00–16:00 PT. Peak bursts can last 10–20 minutes.
- For concurrency, 40 is sounds right for chat frontends; batch jobs prefer throughput.
- Streaming is required for user-facing chat (so first-byte latency is important).
- Data residency: must be US only for now.

We can share a sample traffic CSV and a synthetic workload profile (well export by EOD). Also attaching a preliminary load test we ran against a competitor (initial-load-test-summary.csv) so you can see where were coming from.

Hi Sarah — looping in with a few technical points and an initial plan for a short-run load test.

Quick answers to your question on quantization/batching:
- Quantization: 8-bit (FP8/int8 hybrid) profiles can reduce GPU memory and increase throughput with minor quality degradation for most gen workloads; we recommend validating on ~1k prompts from your dataset.
- Batching: small continuous batches (batch size 8-16) often hit a good balance — for streaming, we use sub-batching where first-byte is prioritized and remaining tokens are batched. We can tune the batching window to hit your first-byte <150 ms target.

Proposed load test (what Redwood will run):
1) Synthetic traffic that mirrors your token distribution (use your CSV sample).
2) 30-minute sustained run at 200 rps, with two 15-minute burst windows at 400 rps.
3) Measure: p50/p95/p99 latency, first-byte streaming latency, throughput, GPU utilization, and tail latencies.

Data we need from FintechCo:
- Sample CSV with tokens/request distribution (Sarah mentioned EOD).
- A sample of 50 production prompts for fidelity testing.

Ill spin up a small Dedicated test pool and share the load-test job link. If youd like, we can also run a canary against a hosted variant for a quick baseline.

-Marcus
